findings.reason: the permission gate must key on the `serves_orchestrators` declaration (which already carries the record-the-dispatch behaviour §3 wants), not on the literal name `claude`, or it forks the fence and misses an alias.
findings.text: §3 gates the `claude` backend on its name, but the codebase already declares the orchestrator-carrying lane via `serves_orchestrators` and records such a dispatch through `_dispatch_orchestrator_lane_stop`; the schema says explicitly the orchestrator role is "declared, never inferred from the backend's name" because name-matching "breaks the moment an orchestrator runs elsewhere"

findings.reason: the plan must reuse the row class rather than ship a second actionable predicate that drifts from the fleet display, and it must reconcile the documented deliberate no-narrowing decision or the plan's exit condition contradicts the command it extends.
findings.text: §7's `crew follow --until-actionable` adds a new predicate for a transition that "needs the orchestrator", but ticker.py already owns exactly that classification (`COORDINATOR_KINDS` and the row-class function returning `ROW_COORDINATOR...)`, and the `crew follow` docstring states "there is deliberately no option to narrow to the action states"

findings.reason: a backend's member-model vocabulary belongs in the catalogue owner (which already fills the model/effort/alias keys per backend), and putting a second list in the flight schema leaves two resolution orders for "which model does this backend serve".
findings.text: §2 makes flight backends "each listing their models" without citing the existing model-catalogue layer, which docs/state/reckon/model-catalogue.yaml and CATALOGUE_LAYER already own and describe as "the reckon decision layer for model selection ... family, model, alias, effort, budget group"

findings.reason: three backend-ordering keys (review_fallback, backends[*].fallback, review_excluded_backends) drift apart; the plan should name the single owner that orders review lanes, or state why recovery cannot be extended.
findings.text: §4 adds a new ordered `review_fallback` key and the plan never states why the existing per-backend `fallback` declaration (BackendConfig.fallback, documented as the backend to substitute when held) or the already-landed `review_excluded_backends` cannot carry the ordering

findings.reason: the overlay may be an intentional skill-parsing surface distinct from the agent-facing AGENTS.md, so a reader should confirm the split rather than assume one owner; flagged so the author states which file owns a project's gates.
findings.text: §9 proposes a per-project overlay (for example docs/state/<project>/build.md) for that project's gates and compute placement, but the repo AGENTS.md already carries project-specific gates (the global rules place test-visibility and compute-placement rules there) and is auto-loaded by every agent entering the repo

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the remaining work extends modules that already hide substantial behaviour behind small interfaces (lane_document.read_lane_document, paid_lanes document composition, worker_digest.generate/verify); no new family of shallow wrappers is proposed.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §3 re-implements the orchestrator-lane fence by backend name, §7 re-derives the "needs the orchestrator" predicate from the follower's own row classes, and §2 re-homes a backend's model outside the catalogue that owns model selection.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan searched the lane and review paths it names (lane.json, lane_document.py, paid_lanes.py, recovery._review_lane_candidates, crew-effort routing), but three of its proposed mechanisms land on owners it never cites: the model catalogue layer (reckon/flight.py:56, docs/state/reckon/model-catalogue.yaml), the orchestrator-lane declaration (dispatch.py:4362, `serves_orchestrators`), and the follower's row classes (ticker.py:1070, `COORDINATOR_KINDS`).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §4 adds an ordered `review_fallback` config key beside the existing per-backend `fallback` key (BackendConfig.fallback) and the already-landed `review_excluded_backends`, without saying why recovery._review_lane_candidates cannot be extended to read the existing declaration.
